goal: Determine whether observable within-stream stationarity diagnostics plus persistence improve conditional worst-environment coverage versus pooled conformal correction without observing hidden scenario labels.
feature: For full 240-sample continuation, detrend whole stream and its two 120-sample halves independently with OLS, compute residual lag1 correlation and RMS. Flag shift if |rho_second-rho_first|>0.22 OR ratio of maximum/minimum residual RMS>1.5; cross shift/stable with whole-stream rho medium [.5,.8) vs high >=.8 (low <.5 remains fallback).

calibration.rank: ceil((n+1)*.90) ordered abs(slope estimate - known simulated true slope)/HAC SE
calibration.unseen_group: Fallback global when calibration group has fewer than 30 entries or is absent.

pilot.disclosure: Negative pilot inspected; parameters unchanged and frozen before final holdout.

comparison: Pooled multiplier learned from SG045's own 360 calibration rows versus observable stationarity/persistence group-specific multipliers; both use same full 240 observations, HAC lag3, 10-sample medians, and SG043 loss model.
metrics: overall and per-scenario true slope coverage
limitations: Full240 feature uses whole continuation and is retrospective, not predecision streaming.
Calibration data from same known synthetic families, only seeds unseen.
Hidden true slopes used to evaluate and calibrate synthetic intervals, not provided to policy.
Pooled split-quantile coverage does not guarantee worst-scenario coverage or conditional validity.
